73:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Muzzammil Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Amr bin Abdul Khaliq Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad bin Musa Al-Qattan Al-Wasiti narrated to us, Ma’la bin Abdul Rahman narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Quraysh gathered in Dar Al-Nadwa and said: Give this man a name that will turn people away from him. They said: A soothsayer. They said: He is not a soothsayer. They said: A madman. They said: He is not mad. They said: A magician. They said: He is not a magician. The polytheists dispersed upon that. report of that reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he wrapped himself in his clothes and covered himself with them. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: O you wrapped up in your garments! “O you wrapped up in your cloak!” Then Al-Bazzar said: A group of scholars narrated from Ma’la bin Abdul Rahman and they accepted his hadith, but he is the only one who narrated hadiths that are not corroborated. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty commands His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to abandon covering himself at night and to rise to stand for the sake of his Lord, the Almighty, as He says: Their sides forsake their beds, to invoke their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend out of what We have provided them. Likewise, the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, was obedient to what God the Almighty commanded him to do regarding standing at night. It was obligatory for him alone, as God the Almighty says: “And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.” Here, He explained to him the amount of time he should stand, as God the Almighty said: O you who is wrapped up in garments, arise during the night, except for a little. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: O you who is wrapped up in garments means O you who sleeps. Qatada said: The one who is wrapped up is in his clothes. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: It was revealed while he was wrapped in a blanket. Shabib bin Bishr said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: O you who is wrapped in a blanket, he said: O Muhammad, you have wrapped yourself in the Qur’an. And the Almighty’s saying: Half of it is a substitute for the night, or subtract from it a little * or add to it, meaning we have commanded you to stand in prayer half the night with a little more or a little less, there is no blame on you for that. God the Almighty said: And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation. This means recite it slowly, as this will help in understanding and contemplating the Qur’an. This is how the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: He used to recite a surah with measured recitation, so that it would be longer than previous ones. In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is narrated on the authority of Anas that he was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said: It was prolonged, then he would recite ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,’ lengthening ‘In the name of God,’ lengthening ‘Al-Rahman,’ and lengthening ‘Al-Raheem.’ Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah on the authority of Umm Salamah may God be pleased with her that she was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and she said: “He would pause his recitation, verse by verse, ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment.’” Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Dhir, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: It will be said to the reciter of the Qur’an: Recite, ascend, and recite as you used to recite in the world, for your status will be at the last verse you recite. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, and al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. We have already presented at the beginning of the interpretation the hadiths that indicate the desirability of chanting and beautifying the voice when reciting, as it came in the hadith: Adorn the Qur’an with your voices, and He is not one of us who does not chant the Qur’an, and This man has been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David, meaning Abu Musa. Abu Musa said: If I had known that you were hearing my recitation, I would have recited it beautifully for you. And on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “Do not scatter it like scattering sand, nor recite it like the recitation of poetry. Stop at its wonders and move hearts with it, and let none of you be concerned with the end of the surah.” Narrated by al-Baghawi. Al-Bukhari said: Adam told us, Shu’bah told us, Amr ibn Murrah told us: I heard Abu Wa’il say: A man came to Ibn Mas’ud and said: I recited al-Mufassal last night in one rak’ah. He said: “This is like the recitation of poetry. I have recognized the pairings that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to combine.” So he mentioned twenty surahs of al-Mufassal, two surahs in one rak’ah. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: meaning, acting upon it. And it was said: It was heavy at the time of its revelation because of its greatness, as Zayd ibn Thabit, may God be pleased with him, said: It was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while his thigh was on my thigh, and it almost crushed my thigh. Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi’ah narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Walid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: I asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, O Messenger of God, do you sense the revelation? The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “I hear a clanging sound, then I fall silent. Every time revelation is sent to me, I feel that my soul is being taken.” Ahmad alone narrated it. At the beginning of Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yusuf, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, How does the revelation come to you? He said: “Sometimes it comes like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest for me, then it leaves me while I have retained what it says. Sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says.” Aisha said: “I saw the revelation come down to him, peace and blessings be upon him, on an extremely cold day, then it leaves him and his forehead is dripping with sweat.” This is the wording of the hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “Revelation would come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on his mount, and it would strike its humps.” Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, “Whenever revelation came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on his camel, it would lower its humps and could not move until he was relieved.” This is a mursal hadith. The hump is the inside of the neck. Ibn Jarir preferred that it is heavy from both aspects, as Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, just as it is heavy in this world as it will be heavy on the Day of Resurrection in the scales. And the Almighty said: Indeed, the rising of the night is more effective for concurrence and more suitable for speech. Abu Ishaq said, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Nasha’a means to stand up in Abyssinian. Umar, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn al-Zubayr said: The whole night is a rising, and this is what Mujahid and others said. It is said that he rose when he got up at night, and in a narration on the authority of Mujahid: after the evening meal. And this is what Abu Majlaz, Qatadah, Salim, Abu Hazim, and Muhammad bin al-Munkadir said: The purpose is that the rising of the night is its hours and times, and every hour of it is called a rising, which is the sighs. The intended meaning is that standing at night is more in agreement between the heart and the tongue and more comprehensive for recitation. For this reason, the Almighty said: It is more effective for concurrence and more suitable for speech, meaning more comprehensive for the mind in performing the recitation and understanding it than standing during the day, because it is the time when people spread out, the noise of voices, and the times of livelihood. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Ibrahim bin Saeed al-Jawhari told us, Abu Usamah told us, al-A’mash told us that Anas bin Malik recited this verse: Indeed, the rising of the night is more effective for concurrence and more suitable for speech. And I said to him: We only read it and I say it. So he said to him: The most correct, the most upright, the most prepared, and the like are all one. That is why God the Almighty said: Indeed, for you during the day is much exertion. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Ata’ ibn Abi Muslim said: It means free time and sleep. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Abu Malik, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: It means a much voluntary act. Qatadah said: It means free time, desire, and turning over. As-Suddi said: A much prolonged exertion means much voluntary worship. Abdur Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said about the words of God the Almighty: Indeed, for you during the day is much exertion, he said: For your needs, so devote the night to your religion. He said: This was when the night prayer was obligatory, then God the Blessed and Exalted bestowed a favor upon His servants, shortened it, and placed it there, and he recited: Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little, to the end of the verse. Then he recited: “Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it and [so do] a party of those with you. And God measures the night and the day. He knows that you cannot enumerate it, so He has turned to you in forgiveness. So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an. He knows that among you will be sick and others traveling throughout the land seeking of the bounty of God and others fighting in the cause of God. So recite what is easy for you of it.” And God the Almighty said: “And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.” This is what he said as he said. The evidence for this is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, where he said: Yahya told us, Saeed ibn Abi Arubah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Zurarah ibn Awfa, on the authority of Saeed ibn Hisham, that he divorced his wife and then traveled to Madinah to sell a property he owned there and use it for mounts and weapons, then fight the Romans until he died. He met a group of his people, and they told him that six of his people wanted to do that during the time of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). He said: Is there not a good example for you in that? He forbade them from doing that and made them witness to her return. Then he came back to us and told us that he came to Ibn Abbas and asked him about the witr prayer. He said: “Shall I not tell you of the most knowledgeable person on earth about the witr prayer of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him)?” He said: Yes. He said: Go to Aisha and ask her, then come back to me and tell me about her response to you. He said: So I came upon Hakim ibn Aflah and asked him to join her, but he said: I will not come near her. I forbade her from saying anything about these two sects, but she refused to do so. So I made him swear, and he came with me. We entered upon her, and she said: Hakim, and I recognized him. He said: Yes. She said: Who is this with you? He said: Saeed ibn Hisham. She said: Who is Hisham? He said: Ibn Amir. She said: So I asked for mercy for him and said: What a good man Amir was. I said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: Do you not read the Quran? I said: Yes. She said: The character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the Quran. I was about to stand up, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stood up. I said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the standing of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: Do you not read this Surah O you who is wrapped up in a cloak? I said: Yes. She said: God made the night prayer obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions stood for a year until their feet swelled, and God held the end of it in the sky for twelve months, then God revealed the alleviation at the end of this surah, so the night prayer became voluntary after it was obligatory. I intended to get up, but then the witr of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) occurred to me, so I said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the witr of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She said: We used to prepare his siwak and his ablution for him, and God would send him out at whatever time He wished to send him out at night, and he would use a siwak, then perform ablution, then pray eight rak’ahs, and he would not sit during them except at the eighth. He would sit and remember his Lord, the Most High, and supplicate, then he would stand up without saying the salutation. Then he would say, Let’s pray the ninth. Then he would sit and remember God alone, then supplicate to Him, then say the salutation in a way that we could hear. Then he would pray two rak’ahs while sitting after saying the salutation. That is eleven rak’ahs, my son. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) grew old and his flesh had taken over, he prayed seven witr prayers, then prayed two rak’ahs while sitting after saying the salutation. That is nine, my son. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a prayer, he liked to continue with it. And if sleep, pain, or illness distracted him from praying at night, he would pray twelve rak’ahs during the day. I do not know that the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited the entire Qur’an in one night until morning, nor did he fast. A whole month other than Ramadan. So I went to Ibn Abbas and told him her story. He said: You have spoken the truth. If I were to visit her, I would have come to her so that she could speak to me face to face. This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it in full. Muslim included it in his Sahih from the hadith of Qatadah with a similar wording. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, in this meaning Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Zaid bin Al-Hubab told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, Mihran told us, they both said, and the wording is from Ibn Wakee’, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, Muhammad bin Tahla’ told me, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: I used to make a mat for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pray on at night, and the people heard about it and gathered, so he went out looking angry, and he was merciful to them, and he feared that the night prayer would be prescribed for them, so he said: O people, be assigned as much work as you can bear, for God does not tire of reward until you tire of work, and the best of deeds are those that are done consistently. And the Qur’an was revealed: O you who are wrapped up in garments, stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little, half of it, or subtract a little from it, or add to it, until a man would tie a rope and hang on. They remained like that for eight months, and God saw what they sought of His pleasure, so He had mercy on them, so He returned them to the obligatory prayer and abandoned the night prayer. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah al-Rabdhi, who is weak. The hadith is in Sahih without the addition of the revelation of this surah. This context may give the impression that this surah was revealed in Medina, but that is not the case. Rather, it is Meccan. His statement in this context that there were eight months between the revelation of its beginning and end is strange, as it was mentioned previously in Ahmad’s narration that there was a year between them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Samak Al-Hanafi, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: When the first part of Al-Muzzammil was first revealed, they would stand for a time similar to the time they stand in Ramadan, and the period between the beginning and the end of it was close to a year. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Abu Usamah, on his authority. Al-Thawri and Muhammad ibn Bishr Al-Abdi said, both of them on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that there was a year between them. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Waki’, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qays ibn Wahb, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, who said: When the verse, O you wrapped in a cloak, was revealed, they stood for a year until their feet and legs swelled, until the verse, Then recite as much of it as is easy for you, was revealed. He said: Then the people rested. And this is what al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Suddi said. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ubayd God ibn Umar al-Qawariri told us, Muadh ibn Hisham told us, my father told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Zurarah ibn Awfa, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Hisham, who said: So I said, meaning to Aisha, “Tell us about the standing of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” She said: Do you not read O you who is wrapped in a garment? I said: Yes. She said: It was the standing of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions until their feet swelled, and the last of it was held in the sky for sixteen months, then it was revealed. Muammar said on the authority of Qatada: Perform the night prayer, except for a little means they stood for a year or two until their shins and feet swelled, and God revealed the easing of it later at the end of the surah. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, who is Ibn Jubayr, who said: When God, the Most High, revealed to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, O you wrapped in a garment, he said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, remained in this state for ten years, standing in prayer at night as He had commanded him, and a group of his companions would stand with him. Then God, the Most High, revealed to him after ten years: “Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you. And God measures the night and the day. He knows that you cannot count it, so He has turned to you in forgiveness. So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an. He knows that there will be among you sick and others traveling throughout the land seeking of the bounty of God and others fighting in the way of God. So recite what is easy for you of it and establish prayer.” So God, the Most High, lightened their burden after ten years. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Amr ibn Rafi`, on the authority of Yaqub al-Qummi, with it. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little, half of it or a little less, that this was difficult for the believers, then God the Almighty made it easier for them and had mercy on them, so He revealed after this: “He knows that among you will be ill and others traveling throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God and others fighting in the cause of God. So recite what is easy of it.” So God the Almighty made it easy, and to Him be praise, and did not make it difficult. And His words the Almighty: And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, meaning, remember Him often, devote yourself to Him and devote yourself to His worship when you are free from your occupations and what you need of your worldly affairs, as God the Almighty said: Then when you are free, then strive, meaning when you are free from your occupations, devote yourself to His obedience and worship so that your mind will be free. Ibn Zayd said it with the same meaning or something close to it. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Salih, Atiyyah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, meaning, devote your worship to Him sincerely. Al-Hasan said: Strive and devote yourself to Him. Ibn Jarir said: “It is said of the worshipper that he is a devotee, and from this comes the narrated hadith: He forbade devotion, meaning devotion to worship and abandoning marriage. And the Almighty’s saying: “Lord of the East and the West, there is no god but Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs,” meaning He is the Owner who controls the East and the West, there is no god but Him. And just as You singled Him out for worship, then single Him out for reliance, so take Him as a Disposer of affairs, as the Almighty said in another verse: So worship Him and put your trust in Him, and as He said: You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help, and there are many verses with this meaning in which there is the command to single out worship and obedience to God and to single Him out for reliance.

Ibn Zayd said it with the same meaning or something close to it. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Salih, Atiyyah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, meaning, devote your worship to Him sincerely. Al-Hasan said: Strive and devote yourself to Him. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said: O you who is wrapped up in garments means O you who sleeps. Qatada said: The one who is wrapped up in garments is in his garments. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: It was revealed while he was wrapped in a blanket. Shabib bin Bishr said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: O you who is wrapped in a blanket, he said: O Muhammad, you have wrapped yourself in the Qur’an. And the Almighty’s saying: Half of it is a substitute for the night, or subtract from it a little * or add to it, meaning we have commanded you to stand in prayer half the night with a little more or a little less, there is no blame on you for that. God the Almighty said: And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation. This means recite it slowly, as this will help in understanding and contemplating the Qur’an. This is how the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: He used to recite a surah with measured recitation, so that it would be longer than previous ones. In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is narrated on the authority of Anas that he was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said: It was prolonged, then he would recite ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful,’ lengthening ‘In the name of God,’ lengthening ‘Al-Rahman,’ and lengthening ‘Al-Raheem.’ Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah on the authority of Umm Salamah may God be pleased with her that she was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and she said: “He would pause his recitation, verse by verse, ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ibn Jarir preferred that it is heavy from both aspects, as Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, just as it is heavy in this world as it will be heavy on the Day of Resurrection in the scales. And the Almighty said: Indeed, the rising of the night is more effective for concurrence and more suitable for speech. It is said that he rose when he got up at night, and in a narration on the authority of Mujahid: after the evening meal. And this is what Abu Majlaz, Qatadah, Salim, Abu Hazim, and Muhammad bin al-Munkadir said: The purpose is that the rising of the night is its hours and times, and every hour of it is called a rising, which is the sighs. For this reason, the Almighty said: It is more effective for concurrence and more suitable for speech, meaning more comprehensive for the mind in performing the recitation and understanding it than standing during the day, because it is the time when people spread out, the noise of voices, and the times of livelihood. That is why God the Almighty said: Indeed, for you during the day is much exertion. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Ata’ ibn Abi Muslim said: It means free time and sleep. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Abu Malik, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: It means a much voluntary act. Qatadah said: It means free time, desire, and turning over. As-Suddi said: A much prolonged exertion means much voluntary worship. Abdur Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said about the words of God the Almighty: Indeed, for you during the day is much exertion, he said: For your needs, so devote the night to your religion. He said: This was when the night prayer was obligatory, then God the Blessed and Exalted bestowed a favor upon His servants, shortened it, and placed it there, and he recited: Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little, to the end of the verse. Then he recited: “Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it and [so do] a party of those with you. And God measures the night and the day. He knows that you cannot enumerate it, so He has turned to you in forgiveness. So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an. He knows that among you will be sick and others traveling throughout the land seeking of the bounty of God and others fighting in the cause of God. So recite what is easy for you of it.” And God the Almighty said: “And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.” This is what he said as he said. He met a group of his people, and they told him that six of his people wanted to do that during the time of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). He said: Is there not a good example for you in that? He forbade them from doing that and made them witness to her return. Then he came back to us and told us that he came to Ibn Abbas and asked him about the witr prayer. He said: “Shall I not tell you of the most knowledgeable person on earth about the witr prayer of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him)?” He said: Yes. He said: Go to Aisha and ask her, then come back to me and tell me about her response to you. He said: So I came upon Hakim ibn Aflah and asked him to join her, but he said: I will not come near her. I forbade her from saying anything about these two sects, but she refused to do so. So I made him swear, and he came with me. We entered upon her, and she said: Hakim, and I recognized him. He said: Yes. She said: Who is this with you? He said: Saeed ibn Hisham. She said: Who is Hisham? He said: Ibn Amir. She said: So I asked for mercy for him and said: What a good man Amir was. I said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: Do you not read the Quran? I said: Yes. She said: The character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the Quran. I was about to stand up, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stood up. I said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the standing of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: Do you not read this Surah O you who is wrapped up in a cloak? I said: Yes. She said: God made the night prayer obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions stood for a year until their feet swelled, and God held the end of it in the sky for twelve months, then God revealed the alleviation at the end of this surah, so the night prayer became voluntary after it was obligatory. I intended to get up, but then the witr of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) occurred to me, so I said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the witr of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She said: We used to prepare his siwak and his ablution for him, and God would send him out at whatever time He wished to send him out at night, and he would use a siwak, then perform ablution, then pray eight rak’ahs, and he would not sit during them except at the eighth. He would sit and remember his Lord, the Most High, and supplicate, then he would stand up without saying the salutation. Then he would say, Let’s pray the ninth. Then he would sit and remember God alone, then supplicate to Him, then say the salutation in a way that we could hear. Then he would pray two rak’ahs while sitting after saying the salutation. That is eleven rak’ahs, my son. That is nine, my son. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a prayer, he liked to continue with it. So I went to Ibn Abbas and told him her story. He said: You have spoken the truth. If I were to visit her, I would have come to her so that she could speak to me face to face. And the Qur’an was revealed: O you who are wrapped up in garments, stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little, half of it, or subtract a little from it, or add to it, until a man would tie a rope and hang on. They remained like that for eight months, and God saw what they sought of His pleasure, so He had mercy on them, so He returned them to the obligatory prayer and abandoned the night prayer. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah al-Rabdhi, who is weak. The hadith is in Sahih without the addition of the revelation of this surah. This context may give the impression that this surah was revealed in Medina, but that is not the case. Rather, it is Meccan. His statement in this context that there were eight months between the revelation of its beginning and end is strange, as it was mentioned previously in Ahmad’s narration that there was a year between them. Al-Thawri and Muhammad ibn Bishr Al-Abdi said, both of them on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that there was a year between them. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Waki’, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He knows that there will be among you sick and others traveling throughout the land seeking of the bounty of God and others fighting in the way of God. So recite what is easy for you of it and establish prayer.” So God, the Most High, lightened their burden after ten years. Ibn Zayd said it with the same meaning or something close to it. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Salih, Atiyyah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, meaning, devote your worship to Him sincerely. Al-Hasan said: Strive and devote yourself to Him. Ibn Jarir said: “It is said of the worshipper that he is a devotee, and from this comes the narrated hadith: He forbade devotion, meaning devotion to worship and abandoning marriage. And the Almighty’s saying: “Lord of the East and the West, there is no god but Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs,” meaning He is the Owner who controls the East and the West, there is no god but Him. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment.’” Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Dhir, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: It will be said to the reciter of the Qur’an: Recite, ascend, and recite as you used to recite in the world, for your status will be at the last verse you recite. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, and al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. We have already presented at the beginning of the interpretation the hadiths that indicate the desirability of chanting and beautifying the voice when reciting, as it came in the hadith: Adorn the Qur’an with your voices, and He is not one of us who does not chant the Qur’an, and This man has been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David, meaning Abu Musa. Abu Musa said: If I had known that you were hearing my recitation, I would have recited it beautifully for you. And on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “Do not scatter it like scattering sand, nor recite it like the recitation of poetry. Stop at its wonders and move hearts with it, and let none of you be concerned with the end of the surah.” Narrated by al-Baghawi. Al-Bukhari said: Adam told us, Shu’bah told us, Amr ibn Murrah told us: I heard Abu Wa’il say: A man came to Ibn Mas’ud and said: I recited al-Mufassal last night in one rak’ah. He said: “This is like the recitation of poetry. I have recognized the pairings that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to combine.” So he mentioned twenty surahs of al-Mufassal, two surahs in one rak’ah. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: meaning, acting upon it. And it was said: It was heavy at the time of its revelation because of its greatness, as Zayd ibn Thabit, may God be pleased with him, said: It was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while his thigh was on my thigh, and it almost crushed my thigh. Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi’ah narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Walid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: I asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, O Messenger of God, do you sense the revelation? The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “I hear a clanging sound, then I fall silent. Every time revelation is sent to me, I feel that my soul is being taken.” Ahmad alone narrated it. At the beginning of Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yusuf, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, How does the revelation come to you? He said: “Sometimes it comes like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest for me, then it leaves me while I have retained what it says. Sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says.” Aisha said: “I saw the revelation come down to him, peace and blessings be upon him, on an extremely cold day, then it leaves him and his forehead is dripping with sweat.” This is the wording of the hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “Revelation would come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on his mount, and it would strike its humps.” Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, “Whenever revelation came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on his camel, it would lower its humps and could not move until he was relieved.” This is a mursal hadith. The hump is the inside of the neck. Ibn Jarir preferred that it is heavy from both aspects, as Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, just as it is heavy in this world as it will be heavy on the Day of Resurrection in the scales. And the Almighty said: Indeed, the rising of the night is more effective for concurrence and more suitable for speech. Abu Ishaq said, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Nasha’a means to stand up in Abyssinian. Umar, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn al-Zubayr said: The whole night is a rising, and this is what Mujahid and others said. It is said that he rose when he got up at night, and in a narration on the authority of Mujahid: after the evening meal. And this is what Abu Majlaz, Qatadah, Salim, Abu Hazim, and Muhammad bin al-Munkadir said: The purpose is that the rising of the night is its hours and times, and every hour of it is called a rising, which is the sighs. The intended meaning is that standing at night is more in agreement between the heart and the tongue and more comprehensive for recitation. For this reason, the Almighty said: It is more effective for concurrence and more suitable for speech, meaning more comprehensive for the mind in performing the recitation and understanding it than standing during the day, because it is the time when people spread out, the noise of voices, and the times of livelihood. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Ibrahim bin Saeed al-Jawhari told us, Abu Usamah told us, al-A’mash told us that Anas bin Malik recited this verse: Indeed, the rising of the night is more effective for concurrence and more suitable for speech. And I said to him: We only read it and I say it. So he said to him: The most correct, the most upright, the most prepared, and the like are all one. That is why God the Almighty said: Indeed, for you during the day is much exertion. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Ata’ ibn Abi Muslim said: It means free time and sleep. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Abu Malik, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: It means a much voluntary act. Qatadah said: It means free time, desire, and turning over. As-Suddi said: A much prolonged exertion means much voluntary worship. Abdur Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said about the words of God the Almighty: Indeed, for you during the day is much exertion, he said: For your needs, so devote the night to your religion. He said: This was when the night prayer was obligatory, then God the Blessed and Exalted bestowed a favor upon His servants, shortened it, and placed it there, and he recited: Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little, to the end of the verse. Then he recited: “Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it and [so do] a party of those with you. And God measures the night and the day. He knows that you cannot enumerate it, so He has turned to you in forgiveness. So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an. He knows that among you will be sick and others traveling throughout the land seeking of the bounty of God and others fighting in the cause of God. So recite what is easy for you of it.” And God the Almighty said: “And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.” This is what he said as he said. The evidence for this is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, where he said: Yahya told us, Saeed ibn Abi Arubah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Zurarah ibn Awfa, on the authority of Saeed ibn Hisham, that he divorced his wife and then traveled to Madinah to sell a property he owned there and use it for mounts and weapons, then fight the Romans until he died. He met a group of his people, and they told him that six of his people wanted to do that during the time of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). He said: Is there not a good example for you in that? He forbade them from doing that and made them witness to her return. Then he came back to us and told us that he came to Ibn Abbas and asked him about the witr prayer. He said: “Shall I not tell you of the most knowledgeable person on earth about the witr prayer of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him)?” He said: Yes. He said: Go to Aisha and ask her, then come back to me and tell me about her response to you. He said: So I came upon Hakim ibn Aflah and asked him to join her, but he said: I will not come near her. I forbade her from saying anything about these two sects, but she refused to do so. So I made him swear, and he came with me. We entered upon her, and she said: Hakim, and I recognized him. He said: Yes. She said: Who is this with you? He said: Saeed ibn Hisham. She said: Who is Hisham? He said: Ibn Amir. She said: So I asked for mercy for him and said: What a good man Amir was. I said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: Do you not read the Quran? I said: Yes. She said: The character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the Quran. I was about to stand up, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stood up. I said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the standing of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: Do you not read this Surah O you who is wrapped up in a cloak? I said: Yes. She said: God made the night prayer obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions stood for a year until their feet swelled, and God held the end of it in the sky for twelve months, then God revealed the alleviation at the end of this surah, so the night prayer became voluntary after it was obligatory. I intended to get up, but then the witr of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) occurred to me, so I said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the witr of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She said: We used to prepare his siwak and his ablution for him, and God would send him out at whatever time He wished to send him out at night, and he would use a siwak, then perform ablution, then pray eight rak’ahs, and he would not sit during them except at the eighth. He would sit and remember his Lord, the Most High, and supplicate, then he would stand up without saying the salutation. Then he would say, Let’s pray the ninth. Then he would sit and remember God alone, then supplicate to Him, then say the salutation in a way that we could hear. Then he would pray two rak’ahs while sitting after saying the salutation. That is eleven rak’ahs, my son. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) grew old and his flesh had taken over, he prayed seven witr prayers, then prayed two rak’ahs while sitting after saying the salutation. That is nine, my son. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a prayer, he liked to continue with it. And if sleep, pain, or illness distracted him from praying at night, he would pray twelve rak’ahs during the day. I do not know that the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited the entire Qur’an in one night until morning, nor did he fast. A whole month other than Ramadan. So I went to Ibn Abbas and told him her story. He said: You have spoken the truth. If I were to visit her, I would have come to her so that she could speak to me face to face. This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it in full. Muslim included it in his Sahih from the hadith of Qatadah with a similar wording. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, in this meaning Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Zaid bin Al-Hubab told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, Mihran told us, they both said, and the wording is from Ibn Wakee’, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, Muhammad bin Tahla’ told me, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: I used to make a mat for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pray on at night, and the people heard about it and gathered, so he went out looking angry, and he was merciful to them, and he feared that the night prayer would be prescribed for them, so he said: O people, be assigned as much work as you can bear, for God does not tire of reward until you tire of work, and the best of deeds are those that are done consistently. And the Qur’an was revealed: O you who are wrapped up in garments, stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little, half of it, or subtract a little from it, or add to it, until a man would tie a rope and hang on. They remained like that for eight months, and God saw what they sought of His pleasure, so He had mercy on them, so He returned them to the obligatory prayer and abandoned the night prayer. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah al-Rabdhi, who is weak. The hadith is in Sahih without the addition of the revelation of this surah. This context may give the impression that this surah was revealed in Medina, but that is not the case. Rather, it is Meccan. His statement in this context that there were eight months between the revelation of its beginning and end is strange, as it was mentioned previously in Ahmad’s narration that there was a year between them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Samak Al-Hanafi, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: When the first part of Al-Muzzammil was first revealed, they would stand for a time similar to the time they stand in Ramadan, and the period between the beginning and the end of it was close to a year. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Abu Usamah, on his authority. Al-Thawri and Muhammad ibn Bishr Al-Abdi said, both of them on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that there was a year between them. Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Waki’, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qays ibn Wahb, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, who said: When the verse, O you wrapped in a cloak, was revealed, they stood for a year until their feet and legs swelled, until the verse, Then recite as much of it as is easy for you, was revealed. He said: Then the people rested. And this is what al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Suddi said. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ubayd God ibn Umar al-Qawariri told us, Muadh ibn Hisham told us, my father told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Zurarah ibn Awfa, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Hisham, who said: So I said, meaning to Aisha, “Tell us about the standing of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” She said: Do you not read O you who is wrapped in a garment? I said: Yes. She said: It was the standing of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions until their feet swelled, and the last of it was held in the sky for sixteen months, then it was revealed. Muammar said on the authority of Qatada: Perform the night prayer, except for a little means they stood for a year or two until their shins and feet swelled, and God revealed the easing of it later at the end of the surah. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, who is Ibn Jubayr, who said: When God, the Most High, revealed to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, O you wrapped in a garment, he said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, remained in this state for ten years, standing in prayer at night as He had commanded him, and a group of his companions would stand with him. Then God, the Most High, revealed to him after ten years: “Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you. And God measures the night and the day. He knows that you cannot count it, so He has turned to you in forgiveness. So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an. He knows that there will be among you sick and others traveling throughout the land seeking of the bounty of God and others fighting in the way of God. So recite what is easy for you of it and establish prayer.” So God, the Most High, lightened their burden after ten years. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Amr ibn Rafi`, on the authority of Yaqub al-Qummi, with it. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: Stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little, half of it or a little less, that this was difficult for the believers, then God the Almighty made it easier for them and had mercy on them, so He revealed after this: “He knows that among you will be ill and others traveling throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God and others fighting in the cause of God. So recite what is easy of it.” So God the Almighty made it easy, and to Him be praise, and did not make it difficult. And His words the Almighty: And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, meaning, remember Him often, devote yourself to Him and devote yourself to His worship when you are free from your occupations and what you need of your worldly affairs, as God the Almighty said: Then when you are free, then strive, meaning when you are free from your occupations, devote yourself to His obedience and worship so that your mind will be free. Ibn Zayd said it with the same meaning or something close to it. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Salih, Atiyyah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, meaning, devote your worship to Him sincerely. Al-Hasan said: Strive and devote yourself to Him. Ibn Jarir said: “It is said of the worshipper that he is a devotee, and from this comes the narrated hadith: He forbade devotion, meaning devotion to worship and abandoning marriage. And the Almighty’s saying: “Lord of the East and the West, there is no god but Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs,” meaning He is the Owner who controls the East and the West, there is no god but Him. And just as You singled Him out for worship, then single Him out for reliance, so take Him as a Disposer of affairs, as the Almighty said in another verse: So worship Him and put your trust in Him, and as He said: You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help, and there are many verses with this meaning in which there is the command to single out worship and obedience to God and to single Him out for reliance.
73:10: God Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be patient with what the fools of his people say of his lies, and to abandon them with a beautiful abandonment, for He is the One with whom there is no reproach. Then He said to him, threatening and warning the infidels of his people, for He is the Great One whose anger cannot be resisted: And leave Me and the deniers of wealth, meaning leave Me and the deniers of luxury, the wealthy, for they are more capable of obedience than others, and they demand rights that others do not have. And grant them respite for a little, meaning slowly, as God Almighty said: We will grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will compel them to a severe punishment. For this reason He said here: Indeed, with Us are shackles, which are the chains, as Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Tawus, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Abdullah ibn Buraydah, Abu Imran al-Jawni, Abu Majlaz, al-Dahhak, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Thawri, and more than one, and a Hellfire, which is the blazing fire, and food of a kind. “A lump in the throat.” Ibn Abbas said: It sticks in the throat, so it neither enters nor exits. “And a painful torment * On the Day the earth and the mountains shake,” meaning they quake, and the mountains become heaps of sand, meaning they become like sand dunes after they were solid stones, then they are blown away and nothing remains of them except gone, until the earth becomes a flat, level plain where you will not see any crookedness, meaning no valley, nor any hill, meaning nothing will descend and nothing will rise. Then the Almighty said, addressing the infidels of Quraysh, and what is meant is all al-Nas 114:Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness over you, meaning over your deeds, “just as We sent to Pharaoh a Messenger. But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a terrible punishment.” Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ath-Thawri said: A terrible punishment, meaning severe. So beware of disbelieving in this Messenger, lest what befell Pharaoh befall you, for God seized him with a mighty, powerful seizure, as the Almighty said: So God seized him as a punishment for the Hereafter and the first time. And you are more deserving of destruction and devastation if You have lied about your Messenger, because your Messenger is more honorable and greater than Moses, son of Imran. It is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. God the Almighty said: Then how can you guard yourself, if you disbelieve, against a Day that will turn the children gray-haired? It is possible that day is the object of to guard yourself as Ibn Jarir narrated from the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud. So how can you, O people, fear a Day that will turn the children gray-haired if you disbelieve in God and do not believe in Him? Or it is possible that it is the object of to disbelieve. Based on the first, how can you be safe from this great terror if you disbelieve? Based on the second, how can you be righteous if you disbelieve in the Day of Resurrection and reject it? Both have good meanings, but the first is better, and God knows best. The meaning of His statement, A Day that will turn the children gray-haired is from the severity of its terrors, earthquakes, and trials. That will be when God the Almighty says to Adam, Send a deputation to Hellfire. He says, From how many? He says, Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine will go to Hellfire and one to Paradise. Al-Tabarani said: Yahya bin Ayoub Al-Alaaf told us, Saeed bin Abi Maryam told us, Nafi bin Yazid told us, Uthman bin Ata Al-Khurasani told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: A Day when children will turn gray, and said: “That is the Day of Resurrection, and that is the Day when God will say to Adam, ‘Arise and send from your descendants a company to the Fire.’ He will say, ‘How many, O Lord?’ He said, ‘From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine, and one will be saved.’ That was difficult for the Muslims, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recognized that. Then he said when he saw that in their faces, ‘The children of Adam are many, and Gog and Magog are from the children of Adam, and not a man of them dies until a thousand men spread out to his loins, so among them and among those like them is a paradise for you.’” This is a strange hadith, and we have already mentioned these hadiths at the beginning of Surat Al-Hajj. And the Almighty’s saying: The sky will be split by it. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: meaning because of it, due to its severity and horror. Some of them attribute the pronoun to God Almighty. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, but it is not strong because it was not mentioned here. And the Almighty’s saying: His promise will be fulfilled, meaning the promise of this day will be fulfilled, meaning it will inevitably happen and will be present and there is no escape from it.

And grant them respite for a little, meaning slowly, as God Almighty said: We will grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will compel them to a severe punishment. For this reason He said here: Indeed, with Us are shackles, which are the chains, as Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Tawus, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Abdullah ibn Buraydah, Abu Imran al-Jawni, Abu Majlaz, al-Dahhak, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Thawri, and more than one, and a Hellfire, which is the blazing fire, and food of a kind. “A lump in the throat.” Ibn Abbas said: It sticks in the throat, so it neither enters nor exits. “And a painful torment * On the Day the earth and the mountains shake,” meaning they quake, and the mountains become heaps of sand, meaning they become like sand dunes after they were solid stones, then they are blown away and nothing remains of them except gone, until the earth becomes a flat, level plain where you will not see any crookedness, meaning no valley, nor any hill, meaning nothing will descend and nothing will rise. Then the Almighty said, addressing the infidels of Quraysh, and what is meant is all al-Nas 114:Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness over you, meaning over your deeds, “just as We sent to Pharaoh a Messenger. But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a terrible punishment.” Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ath-Thawri said: A terrible punishment, meaning severe. So beware of disbelieving in this Messenger, lest what befell Pharaoh befall you, for God seized him with a mighty, powerful seizure, as the Almighty said: So God seized him as a punishment for the Hereafter and the first time. And you are more deserving of destruction and devastation if You have lied about your Messenger, because your Messenger is more honorable and greater than Moses, son of Imran. It is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. God the Almighty said: Then how can you guard yourself, if you disbelieve, against a Day that will turn the children gray-haired? It is possible that day is the object of to guard yourself as Ibn Jarir narrated from the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud. So how can you, O people, fear a Day that will turn the children gray-haired if you disbelieve in God and do not believe in Him? Or it is possible that it is the object of to disbelieve. Based on the first, how can you be safe from this great terror if you disbelieve? Based on the second, how can you be righteous if you disbelieve in the Day of Resurrection and reject it? Both have good meanings, but the first is better, and God knows best. The meaning of His statement, A Day that will turn the children gray-haired is from the severity of its terrors, earthquakes, and trials. That will be when God the Almighty says to Adam, Send a deputation to Hellfire. He says, From how many? He says, Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine will go to Hellfire and one to Paradise. Al-Tabarani said: Yahya bin Ayoub Al-Alaaf told us, Saeed bin Abi Maryam told us, Nafi bin Yazid told us, Uthman bin Ata Al-Khurasani told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: A Day when children will turn gray, and said: “That is the Day of Resurrection, and that is the Day when God will say to Adam, ‘Arise and send from your descendants a company to the Fire.’ He will say, ‘How many, O Lord?’ He said, ‘From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine, and one will be saved.’ That was difficult for the Muslims, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recognized that. Then he said when he saw that in their faces, ‘The children of Adam are many, and Gog and Magog are from the children of Adam, and not a man of them dies until a thousand men spread out to his loins, so among them and among those like them is a paradise for you.’” This is a strange hadith, and we have already mentioned these hadiths at the beginning of Surat Al-Hajj. And the Almighty’s saying: The sky will be split by it. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: meaning because of it, due to its severity and horror. Some of them attribute the pronoun to God Almighty. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, but it is not strong because it was not mentioned here. And the Almighty’s saying: His promise will be fulfilled, meaning the promise of this day will be fulfilled, meaning it will inevitably happen and will be present and there is no escape from it.
73:19: God the Almighty says: Indeed, this meaning the Surah is a reminder meaning that those with understanding will remember by it. For this reason, God the Almighty said: So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way meaning whoever God the Almighty wills to guide, as He has specified in the other Surah. “And you do not will except that God wills. Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise.” Then God the Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you meaning sometimes like this and sometimes like that, and all of this is without your intention, but you are not able to persevere in what He has commanded you of standing at night because it is difficult for you. For this reason, He said: And God determines the night and the day meaning sometimes they are equal and sometimes He takes this from this and that from that He knows that you will not be able to enumerate it meaning the obligation that He has made obligatory upon you. So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an meaning without specifying a time, meaning, but stand during the night as much as is easy. He expressed prayer by recitation as He said in Surah Subhan: And do not recite your prayer aloud meaning By your recitation, And do not lower your voice therein. The companions of Imam Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, used this verse, which says: So recite whatever is easy for you of the Qur’an, as evidence that it is not necessary to recite Al-Fatihah in prayer. Rather, if one recites it or another verse from the Qur’an, even if it is just one verse, it is sufficient for him. They supported this with the hadith of the one who performed his prayer incorrectly, which is in the two Sahihs: Then recite whatever is easy for you of the Qur’an. The majority responded to them with the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, which is also in the two Sahihs, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no prayer for the one who does not recite Al-Fatihah. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every prayer in which the Mother of the Qur’an is not recited is deficient, deficient, incomplete. In Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, The prayer of the one who does not recite the Mother of the Qur’an is not sufficient. God the Almighty said: He knows that among you will be sick and others traveling throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God and others fighting in the cause of God. That is, He knew that among this nation there will be those who have excuses for not praying at night, such as those who are sick and unable to do so, and travelers in the land seeking from the bounty of God in earnings and trade, and others who will be busy with what is more important to them than fighting in the cause of God. This verse, indeed the entire surah, was revealed in Mecca, and fighting had not yet been legislated. It is one of the greatest proofs of prophethood, because it is a form of informing of future unseen matters. For this reason, God the Almighty said: So recite what is easy for you from it. That is, do what is easy for you from it. Ibn Jarir said: Ya`qub told us, Ibn `Ulayyah told us on the authority of Abu Raja` Muhammad, who said: I said to Al-Hasan: O Abu Sa`id, what do you say about a man who has memorized the entire Qur’an by heart but does not perform it, but only prays the obligatory prayers? He said: He uses the Qur’an as a pillow. May God curse that one. God the Most High said to the righteous servant: And indeed, he is full of knowledge because of what We taught him and And you have been taught that which neither you nor your fathers knew. I said: O Abu Sa`id, God the Most High said: So recite whatever is easy for you of the Qur’an. He said: Yes, even if it is five verses. This is apparent from the school of thought of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, that he saw it as a right and obligation upon those who carry the Qur’an to perform the night prayer, even if it is only part of it. For this reason it is stated in the hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who slept until morning, and he said: That is a man in whose ear the devil urinated. It was said that it means he slept through the obligatory prayers, and it was said about the night prayer: In the Sunnah: Perform the witr prayer, O people of the Qur’an. And in another hadith: Whoever does not perform the witr prayer is not one of us. Stranger than this is what was reported on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn `Abd Al-`Aziz from the Hanbalis from The positive aspect of Ramadan is that it is obligatory. And God knows best. Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad bin Saeed Farqad Al-Hadrad told us, Abu Muhammad bin Yusuf Al-Zubaidi told us, Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Tawus from the descendants of Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Recite as much of it as is easy for you. He said: One hundred verses. This is a very strange hadith that I only saw in the Mu’jam of Al-Tabarani, may God have mercy on him. And the words of God Almighty: And establish prayer and give zakat mean: establish your obligatory prayers and give the obligatory zakat. This indicates for those who say that the obligation of zakat was revealed in Makkah, but the amounts of the zakat and the amount of the tax were not made clear until Madinah, and God knows best. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and more than one of the early Muslims said: This verse abrogated what God had first obligated upon the Muslims, namely, the night prayer. They differed regarding the period of time between them, as mentioned above. It has been proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to that man: Five prayers during the day and night. He said: Do I have to do anything else? He said: No, unless you do it voluntarily. God the Almighty says: And loan God a goodly loan meaning from charity, for God will reward you for that with the best and most abundant reward, as God the Almighty says: Who is it that will loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? And He the Almighty says: And whatever good you send forth for yourselves - you will find it with God, better and greater in reward. That is, everything you send forth before you is for you and is better than what you kept for yourselves in this world. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Abu Khaithama told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Suwayd, who said: Abdullah said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Which of you loves his own wealth more than the wealth of his heir? They said: O Messenger of God, there is none of us but loves his own wealth more than the wealth of his heir. He said: Know what you are saying. They said: We do not know anything except that, O Messenger of God? He said: The wealth of one of you is what he has sent forward, and the wealth of his heir is what he has left behind. Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Hafs ibn Ghiyath, and al-Nasa’i narrated it from the path of Abu Mu’awiyah, both of them from al-A’mash with this chain of transmission. Then God the Almighty said: “And seek forgiveness of God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” That is, remember Him often and seek His forgiveness in all your affairs, for He is Forgiving and Merciful to whoever seeks His forgiveness. The end of the interpretation of Surat al-Muzzammil. Praise and thanks be to God.
